title: Prenatal exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals in relation to thyroid hormone levels in infants - a Dutch prospective cohort study.
ehr_evidence: information on T4 levels in heel prick blood spots was obtained through the neonatal screening programme in the Netherlands.
summary: Prospective cohort study assessing the association between prenatal exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) and thyroxine (T4) levels in newborns in the Netherlands.
key_findings: Girls in the highest quartile of DDE exposure showed significantly increased T4 levels compared to the lowest quartile (+24.8 nmol/L, 95% CI 0.79, 48.75; p=0.043).
Girls in the highest quartile of PFOA exposure showed significantly increased T4 levels compared to the lowest quartile (+38.6 nmol/L, 95% CI 13.34, 63.83; p=0.004).
Boys in the second quartile of PFOS and PFOA exposure had lower T4 levels in crude models, but associations were attenuated and non-significant after full adjustment.
No significant associations were observed for DEHP metabolites, PCB-153, or HCB.
captured_features: T4 levels from heel prick blood spots
DDE, PFOS, PFOA, PCB-153, HCB, DEHP metabolites in cord plasma and breast milk
limitations: reduced statistical power due to quartile and gender stratification
lack of thyroid binding protein data
